item.title: Shell
item.description:
A POSIX shell for WASI containers, in pure Go, built for GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm: go-wasmcontainers/shell. It is what makes shell-form commands work: RUN a && b in a Containerfile, wctr run IMAGE sh -c '…', and wctr exec -it CONTAINER sh.

A WebAssembly module cannot start another program: Go’s port has no fork or exec, and WASI preview 1 has no process calls. So the shell uses a small subset of WASIX, in WASIX’s own import module (wasix_32v1): proc_spawn3, proc_join, fd_pipe, proc_id, proc_parent, tty_get and tty_set, and nothing else (no fork, exec, threads or signals). The engine serves that subset from v0.17.0 (wctrd --wasi engine, the default): see Architecture.

Status: shell v0.1.0 is released. sh runs on the engine, where pipelines through the coreutils work. The base image is ghcr.io/go-wasmcontainers/shell:0.1.0 (wasip1/wasm, one layer): /bin/sh, /bin/coreutils.wasm (the multicall module of wasmdesk/coreutils, released as v0.4.0, with 42 tools as symbolic links), a root-only /etc/passwd, and the config Shell ["/bin/sh","-c"], which is what a shell-form RUN runs. The image’s registry package is not public yet (it becomes public soon); until then it cannot be pulled without access.

  • wasix: //go:wasmimport bindings for the subset, with a Go API.
  • sh: the mvdan.cc/sh v3.14.1 interpreter (patched with one change: a pipe function, since upstream’s os.Pipe is ENOSYS on wasip1), whose external commands start with proc_spawn3.

sh does pipelines, redirections, here-documents, command substitution, cd, exported variables, $?, set -e/-u/-x/-f/-a, exec, sh -c, sh file and an interactive prompt on a TTY. By design of the subset it has no signals, no job control and no process substitution.
